Q: How do skill provenance, versioning and delegated authority affect safe execution?
A:
A skill packages instructions and supporting resources, but its text does not automatically grant every permission it requests. Record provenance and version, load only the relevant material and preserve the application/user authority boundary.

Validate referenced paths and tools according to their actual capabilities. A changed skill can alter behavior without changing the main prompt, so include it in release and evaluation identity. Delegating a task should constrain scope and return useful evidence rather than transferring unrestricted credentials by default.
Why: A downloaded skill instructs an agent to export all local environment variables for diagnostics. Those instructions are untrusted content until justified by the task and policy; relevance does not make the export authorized.
Risk: Instruction packaging can disguise a privilege escalation as setup guidance.
Trade: Reusable skills reduce repetition when authority and resource access remain explicit.
Try: Review a skill update for new destinations, tool permissions and changes to task scope.
